_about: Prose for Kestrel Pay's generated history (task K6), written once by an LLM (Claude) and committed. history/generate.py only reads this file and makes no API calls. Incident text uses {placeholders} that generate.py fills (ids, versions, people, alert values). incidents[kind][n] is the text for the n-th incident of that kind.

checkout_bad_deploy.title: checkout-api 5xx after {version} deploy
checkout_bad_deploy.summary: checkout-api failed {a0} of requests after {deploy} ({version}) switched cart serialization to orjson, which cannot encode Decimal prices on discounted carts. Rolled back to {prev_version}.
checkout_bad_deploy.commit: Serialize cart line items with orjson for faster totals
timeline: Alert: checkout-api error rate {a0} (threshold 1%). Incident opened.
{resolver_first} sees 'TypeError: Decimal is not JSON serializable' in checkout-api logs, starting right after {deploy}.
Roll back {deploy} rather than hotfix: every cart with a discount code hits the error.
Error rate under 0.2% for 8 minutes. Resolved.

postmortem.title: checkout-api errors from orjson cart serialization
postmortem.body:
## Summary
For {duration} minutes checkout-api failed {a0} of requests after {deploy} ({version}) switched cart serialization to orjson.

## Impact
Shoppers using a discount code could not check out. Nobody was charged twice.

## Root cause
Commit {sha} by {cause_author} serialized line item prices with orjson, which does not encode Decimal. Carts without discounts carry float prices and worked, so the unit tests passed.

## Resolution
{resolver} rolled checkout-api back to {prev_version}.

## Follow-ups
- Add a discounted cart to the checkout-api contract tests.
- Represent money as integer cents everywhere in checkout-api.

checkout_bad_deploy.title: checkout-api failing every checkout after {version}
checkout_bad_deploy.summary: {deploy} ({version}) pointed checkout-api's pricing client at a pricing-svc v2 endpoint that did not exist yet; every price lookup returned 404 and checkout-api failed {a0} of requests. Rolled back.
checkout_bad_deploy.commit: Move pricing-svc client to the v2 quote endpoint
timeline: Alert: checkout-api error rate {a0}. Sev1 opened: checkout is effectively down.
checkout-api logs 404 from pricing-svc on /v2/quotes; pricing-svc itself is healthy.
{deploy} went out {lag} minutes before the alert and changed the pricing client.
Roll back {deploy}: pricing-svc has not shipped v2 yet.
Checkout success rate back to normal. Resolved.

postmortem.title: checkout-api called a pricing-svc endpoint that did not exist yet
postmortem.body:
## Summary
Checkout failed for {duration} minutes ({a0} errors) because {deploy} called pricing-svc's v2 quote endpoint before pricing-svc shipped it.

## Impact
Most checkouts failed during the window; shoppers saw "unable to price cart".

## Root cause
Commit {sha} by {cause_author} assumed the pricing-svc v2 rollout had finished. The two changes were coordinated in chat, not in the deploy pipeline.

## Resolution
Rolled back to {prev_version}.

## Follow-ups
- Contract test between checkout-api and pricing-svc in CI.
- Put client switches to new upstream endpoints behind a flag.

checkout_bad_deploy.title: checkout-api p99 latency over 3 s after {version}

checkout_bad_deploy.commit: Re-check stock for each line item before starting payment
timeline: Traces show one inventory-svc call per cart line, in sequence; inventory-svc answers each in 15 ms.
The per-line re-check came in {deploy}, deployed {lag} minutes before the alert.

postmortem.title: Per-line stock re-check made large carts slow
postmortem.body:
## Summary
checkout-api p99 latency reached {a0} for {duration} minutes after {deploy} ({version}) re-checked stock once per cart line.

## Impact
Carts with more than 20 lines took over 3 seconds to start payment; some shoppers abandoned.

## Root cause
Commit {sha} by {cause_author} called inventory-svc in a loop. inventory-svc already has a batch endpoint.

## Resolution
Rolled back to {prev_version}.

## Follow-ups
- Use the inventory-svc batch reservation check.
- Add a 50-line cart to the checkout-api load test.

checkout_bad_deploy.summary: {deploy} ({version}) offered saved cards on every cart; guest carts have no customer id and checkout-api raised KeyError on {a0} of requests. Rolled back.
checkout_bad_deploy.commit: Offer saved cards on the payment step for all carts
timeline: "KeyError: 'customer_id'" in the payment step; only guest carts are affected.
{deploy} by {cause_first} changed the saved-cards query {lag} minutes before the alert.
Roll back instead of turning off enable_saved_cards: the flag also gates signed-in shoppers.

postmortem.title: Saved cards broke guest checkout
postmortem.body:
## Summary
Guest checkouts failed for {duration} minutes ({a0} of requests) after {deploy} ({version}) offered saved cards on every cart.

## Impact
Guest shoppers, about a third of checkout traffic, could not pay.

## Root cause
Commit {sha} by {cause_author} read customer_id from every cart; guest carts do not have one. Tests only used signed-in fixtures.

## Resolution
Rolled back to {prev_version}.

## Follow-ups
- Guest cart fixture in the checkout-api test suite.
- Split enable_saved_cards into per-audience flags.

checkout_bad_deploy.title: checkout-api 'cart not found' errors after {version}
checkout_bad_deploy.summary: {deploy} ({version}) read cart_ttl_s through a settings loader that treats durations as milliseconds; carts expired in redis-cache after 1.8 seconds and {a0} of checkouts failed. Rolled back.
checkout_bad_deploy.commit: Read cart TTL through the shared settings loader
timeline: Errors are 'cart not found'. redis-cache is healthy, but cart keys are written with a 1.8 s TTL.
{deploy} moved cart_ttl_s to the shared settings loader, which reads durations as milliseconds.
Carts persist again; error rate normal. Resolved.

postmortem.title: Cart TTL read in the wrong unit
postmortem.body:
## Summary
For {duration} minutes {a0} of checkouts failed with "cart not found" because {deploy} ({version}) set cart TTLs 1000 times too short.

## Impact
Shoppers who took more than two seconds between cart and payment lost their cart.

## Root cause
Commit {sha} by {cause_author} read cart_ttl_s through the shared settings loader, which assumes milliseconds unless the key ends in _ms. The key name says seconds.

## Resolution
Rolled back to {prev_version}. redis-cache was never the problem, though it showed up first in traces.

## Follow-ups
- Make the settings loader honor _s and _ms suffixes.
- Alert on cart key TTL below 60 seconds.

timeline: Alert: checkout-api error rate {a1}. Sev1 opened.

postmortem.title: Northbank authorization latency
postmortem.body:
## Summary
Northbank, our primary acquirer, degraded for about 90 minutes. Charges timed out until we routed traffic to Meridian 14 minutes in.

## Impact
{a1} of checkouts failed for 20 minutes. Meridian costs 0.04% more per transaction while it carries traffic.

## Root cause
External: Northbank authorization latency. No Kestrel Pay change was involved.

## Resolution
{resolver} ran "Route card traffic to the backup acquirer" and switched back once Northbank recovered.

## Follow-ups
- Alert on acquirer latency before checkout errors, so the switch happens sooner.
- Ask Northbank for status page webhooks.

acquirer_outage.title: Northbank declining charges with system errors
acquirer_outage.summary: Northbank returned system errors (response code 96) on {a0} of authorizations and checkout-api errors hit {a1}. Same pattern as {last_same}: switched to Meridian with the runbook within 9 minutes.
timeline: Alert: checkout-api error rate {a1}. Sev1 opened.
Response code 96 (system malfunction) from Northbank only; Meridian test charges pass. Same pattern as {last_same}.
Ran 'Route card traffic to the backup acquirer'.
Checkout error rate back to 0.3% on Meridian.
Northbank confirmed a fix; primary_acquirer switched back to northbank.

postmortem.title: Northbank system errors, second outage
postmortem.body:
## Summary
Northbank failed {a0} of authorizations with response code 96 for about an hour. Second Northbank outage after {last_same}.

## Impact
{a1} of checkouts failed for 12 minutes, until traffic moved to Meridian.

## Root cause
External: a Northbank processor fault.

## Resolution
{resolver} ran "Route card traffic to the backup acquirer" 9 minutes in, faster than {last_same} because the runbook was known.

## Follow-ups
- Automate the acquirer switch when one acquirer's error rate passes 20%.

webhooks_retry_storm.title: Webhook retry storm after max_retries raised to {new}
webhooks_retry_storm.summary: {cause_author} raised webhooks-svc max_retries from {old} to {new} ({cfg}). Deliveries to failing merchant endpoints were retried far more often, delivery p99 hit {a0} and kafka disk reached {a1}. Restored {old} and drained the backlog.
timeline: Alert: kafka saturation {a1}; the webhook retry topic is growing fast.
Retries per delivery up 4x since {cfg} raised max_retries to {new}, {lag} minutes before the first alert.
Ran 'Scale webhooks-svc and drain the delivery backlog'.
Consumer lag under a minute; kafka disk back to 61%. Resolved.

postmortem.title: Raising webhook retries flooded kafka
postmortem.body:
## Summary
{cfg} raised webhooks-svc max_retries from {old} to {new}. Within {lag} minutes retries to dead merchant endpoints dominated delivery and filled the retry topic.

## Impact
Webhook delivery to every merchant slowed to {a0} p99 for about an hour. Kafka disk reached {a1}, close to affecting payment events.

## Root cause
{cause_author} raised retries to help one merchant with a flaky endpoint. Retries are per delivery, so every failing endpoint got the same treatment.

## Resolution
{resolver} restored max_retries to {old} and drained the backlog with the runbook.

## Follow-ups
- Per-merchant retry budgets instead of one global setting.
- Separate disk quota for the webhook retry topic.

search_index_red.summary: {deploy} upgraded search-index to {version}; the new nodes could not read the old shard allocation and the cluster went red. search-api failed {a0} of queries. Rolled back.
search_index_red.commit: Upgrade Elasticsearch to 8.15 and switch to the desired-balance allocator
timeline: search-index cluster health red; 14 primary shards unassigned since {deploy}.

postmortem.title: Elasticsearch upgrade left shards unassigned
postmortem.body:
## Summary
Merchant order search was down for {duration} minutes after {deploy} upgraded search-index to {version}.

## Impact
Dashboard search failed for all merchants ({a0} of queries). Payments were not affected.

## Root cause
Commit {sha} by {cause_author} switched to the desired-balance allocator in the same change as the version upgrade. Mixed-version nodes could not agree on allocation.

## Resolution
Rolled back to {prev_version}; shards reallocated in about 25 minutes.

## Follow-ups
- Upgrade versions and change allocator settings in separate deploys.
- Rehearse search-index upgrades on the staging snapshot.

search_index_red.title: search-index disk flood-stage watermark reached
search_index_red.summary: search-index data nodes passed the flood-stage disk watermark ({a0}) and indices went read-only; search-api failed {a1} of queries. Deleted expired indices and cleared the read-only block.
timeline: Indices are read-only (flood-stage watermark). The 13-month retention job has not run for 3 weeks.
Deleted indices older than 13 months and removed the read-only block.

postmortem.title: search-index retention job silently stopped
postmortem.body:
## Summary
search-index disks filled to {a0} and Elasticsearch made indices read-only, so new transactions could not be indexed and search-api failed {a1} of queries.

## Impact
Merchant search was degraded for {duration} minutes. Tier 3; no payment impact.

## Root cause
The nightly retention job had been failing for three weeks after its credentials rotated. Nobody was alerted.

## Resolution
{resolver} deleted expired indices by hand and cleared the read-only block.

## Follow-ups
- Alert when the retention job has not succeeded for 2 days.
- Disk alert at 80%, well before the flood-stage watermark.

redis_maxmemory.title: Sessions dropped after redis-cache maxmemory cut to {new}
redis_maxmemory.summary: {cause_author} lowered redis-cache maxmemory from {old} to {new} ({cfg}) to make room on the host. Redis evicted session and idempotency keys; auth-svc errors reached {a1} and shoppers were logged out mid-checkout. Restored {old} with the runbook.
timeline: Alert: auth-svc error rate {a1}. Sev1 opened.
evicted_keys climbing by 40k/s. {cfg} cut maxmemory to {new} {lag} minutes before the first alert.
Ran 'Restore redis-cache maxmemory and eviction policy': maxmemory back to {old}.
Evictions stopped; auth-svc owners confirm sessions are stable.
auth-svc and checkout-api error rates normal. Resolved.

postmortem.title: redis-cache maxmemory cut evicted sessions
postmortem.body:
## Summary
{cfg} lowered redis-cache maxmemory from {old} to {new}. Redis started evicting keys at once, including sessions and idempotency keys.

## Impact
For {duration} minutes auth-svc failed {a1} of requests and checkout-api {a2}. Merchants were logged out of the dashboard; some shoppers had to restart checkout.

## Root cause
{cause_author} reduced memory to fit a second Redis on the same host. Everything that uses redis-cache shares one keyspace, so the eviction policy cannot protect sessions.

## Resolution
{resolver} restored maxmemory to {old} with the runbook.

## Follow-ups
- Move sessions to their own Redis with noeviction.
- Alert on evicted_keys, not just memory.

payments_bad_deploy.title: payments-svc rejecting retries as duplicates after {version}
payments_bad_deploy.summary: {deploy} ({version}) derived idempotency keys from the cart id alone, so legitimate retries after a soft decline were rejected as duplicates. payments-svc errors reached {a0}. Rolled back.
payments_bad_deploy.commit: Derive idempotency keys from cart id to simplify retries
timeline: Alert: payments-svc error rate {a0}. Sev1 opened.
Errors are 409 duplicate_request on second attempts; the idempotency key format changed in {deploy}.

postmortem.title: Idempotency keys collided on retries
postmortem.body:
## Summary
For {duration} minutes payments-svc rejected {a0} of charges as duplicates after {deploy} ({version}) changed how idempotency keys are built.

## Impact
Shoppers whose first attempt was soft-declined could not retry with another card. checkout-api errors reached {a1}.

## Root cause
Commit {sha} by {cause_author} keyed idempotency on the cart id only. A retry with a new card is a new payment attempt and needs its own key.

## Resolution
Rolled back to {prev_version}.

## Follow-ups
- Idempotency key = cart id + attempt number.
- Test: soft decline then retry with a different card.

payments_bad_deploy.title: payments-svc latency up after {version} added a second fraud call
payments_bad_deploy.summary: {deploy} ({version}) called fraud-svc twice per charge, before and after authorization; payments-svc p99 rose to {a0}. Rolled back.
payments_bad_deploy.commit: Score charges again after authorization for chargeback signals
timeline: Traces show two fraud-svc calls per charge since {deploy}; fraud-svc itself is within its SLO.

postmortem.title: Second fraud call doubled charge latency
postmortem.body:
## Summary
payments-svc p99 latency reached {a0} for {duration} minutes after {deploy} ({version}) added a post-authorization fraud score.

## Impact
Checkouts were slow; no errors.

## Root cause
Commit {sha} by {cause_author} made the second fraud call synchronous. It only feeds chargeback analytics and can run after the response.

## Resolution
Rolled back to {prev_version}.

## Follow-ups
- Send the post-authorization score through kafka instead of inline.

notifications_provider.title: Receipt emails failing at the email provider
notifications_provider.summary: Postmark returned 503 on {a0} of sends for {duration} minutes. No Kestrel Pay change; queued receipts were sent once the provider recovered.
timeline: 503s from Postmark only; SMS through Twilio unaffected. Postmark's status page shows an outage.
Wait it out: receipts stay queued in kafka and are retried, nothing is lost.

postmortem.title: Postmark outage delayed receipts
postmortem.body:
## Summary
Receipt emails were delayed for {duration} minutes while Postmark was down.

## Impact
Shoppers got receipts late. No emails were lost.

## Root cause
External: Postmark outage.

## Resolution
{resolver} confirmed receipts were buffered in kafka and waited for recovery.

## Follow-ups
- Evaluate a second email provider.

notifications_provider.title: Receipt emails failing again at Postmark
notifications_provider.summary: Second Postmark outage after {last_same}: {a0} of sends failed for {duration} minutes. Receipts were retried from kafka once it recovered.
timeline: No fallback provider is wired up yet; wait for Postmark and let kafka buffer receipts.

postmortem.title: Postmark outage, second time
postmortem.body:
## Summary
Postmark failed {a0} of sends for {duration} minutes, the second outage after {last_same}.

## Impact
Receipts were late; none were lost.

## Root cause
External: Postmark outage. The follow-up from {last_same} (a second provider) was not done.

## Resolution
Waited for recovery; kafka buffered receipts.

## Follow-ups
- Wire SendGrid as a fallback email_provider this quarter.

inventory_index_dropped.title: inventory-svc slow after a migration dropped the reservations index
inventory_index_dropped.summary: {deploy} ({version}) ran a migration that dropped idx_reservations_sku_expires as unused. Reservation lookups became sequential scans; inventory-svc p99 hit {a0} and checkout-api {a1}. Recreated the index concurrently.
timeline: inventory-db CPU at 96%; pg_stat_activity shows sequential scans on stock_reservations.
The migration in {deploy} dropped idx_reservations_sku_expires {lag} minutes before the first alert.
Do not roll back a database deploy (policy no-database-rollback); recreate the index instead.
Ran 'Kill runaway queries and restore the inventory-db index'.
Index rebuilt; inventory-svc p99 back to 22 ms. Resolved.

postmortem.title: Dropping an 'unused' index made inventory-db scan
postmortem.body:
## Summary
{deploy} ({version}) dropped idx_reservations_sku_expires. inventory-db fell back to sequential scans and inventory-svc p99 reached {a0}.

## Impact
Checkouts were slow for {duration} minutes (checkout-api p99 {a1}). No failed payments.

## Root cause
Commit {sha} by {cause_author} dropped indexes reported unused by pg_stat_user_indexes on a replica, where the reservation expiry query never runs.

## Resolution
{resolver} cancelled the runaway queries and recreated the index concurrently with the runbook.

## Follow-ups
- Check index usage on the primary before dropping.
- Review inventory-db migrations with the checkout team.

pool_exhaustion.title: Checkout failing: payments-db connection pool exhausted
pool_exhaustion.summary: {cause_author} lowered payments-db max_pool_size from {old} to {new} ({cfg}) to cut idle connections. At peak payments-svc could not get a connection, charges timed out and checkout-api errors reached {a1}. Failing over did not help; raising max_pool_size back to {old} and restarting payments-svc did.
timeline: Alert: checkout-api error rate {a1}. Sev1 opened.
payments-svc logs 'timeout acquiring connection'; payments-db CPU is only 35%.
Suspect a sick primary: connections pinned at the pool limit although queries are fast.
Ran 'Fail over payments-db to the standby'.
Failover did not help: the standby has the same max_pool_size and filled up within a minute.
{cfg} lowered max_pool_size from {old} to {new} {lag} minutes before the first alert.
Raised max_pool_size back to {old} and restarted payments-svc pod by pod.
Charges succeeding; checkout-api errors under 1% for 10 minutes. Resolved.

postmortem.title: payments-db pool cut to {new} exhausted connections at peak
postmortem.body:
## Summary
For {duration} minutes checkout failed for most shoppers. payments-db's server-side pool was lowered from {old} to {new} ({cfg}); at peak payments-svc needs about 160 connections.

## Impact
{a1} of checkouts failed. Charges that timed out were never captured, so nobody was charged twice.

## Root cause
{cause_author} lowered the pool off-peak to cut idle connections. Config changes to payments-db skip the deploy pipeline and had no review. Every payments-svc pod shares the one pool, so the limit is hit everywhere at once.

## What did not work
Failing over to the standby (minute 21) cost 8 minutes: the standby has the same pool config.

## Resolution
{resolver} raised max_pool_size back to {old} and restarted payments-svc so every pod reconnected.

## Follow-ups
- Alert on pool saturation above 80%, before checkout fails.
- Require a payments review for changes to services/payments-db/config.yaml.
- Write the runbook "Raise pool + restart payments-svc".

pool_exhaustion.title: payments-db pool exhausted again after max_pool_size cut to {new}
pool_exhaustion.summary: Same failure as {last_same}. {cause_author} lowered payments-db max_pool_size from {old} to {new} ({cfg}) to match a pgbouncer default; checkout-api errors reached {a1}. A checkout-api deploy ({decoy_deploy}) {decoy_lag} minutes before the alert looked suspicious but was unrelated. Raised the pool and restarted payments-svc.
timeline: Alert: checkout-api error rate {a1}. Sev1 opened.
checkout-api deployed {decoy_version} ({decoy_deploy}) just before the alert, but its errors are timeouts from payments-svc, not checkout code.
payments-svc waits on connections at the pool limit, same signature as {last_same}. {cfg} lowered max_pool_size to {new}.
Skip the failover (it did not help in {last_same}); go straight to the pool runbook.
Ran 'Raise pool + restart payments-svc': max_pool_size back to {old}.
Checkout errors under 1% for 10 minutes. Resolved.

postmortem.title: payments-db pool exhaustion, second time
postmortem.body:
## Summary
{cfg} lowered payments-db max_pool_size from {old} to {new}, and checkout failed exactly as in {last_same}. Resolved in {duration} minutes with the runbook written after {last_same}.

## Impact
{a1} of checkouts failed for about 15 minutes.

## Root cause
{cause_author} aligned max_pool_size with a pgbouncer default. The review required after {last_same} was not enforced in tooling.

## Red herring
checkout-api {decoy_version} ({decoy_deploy}) shipped {decoy_lag} minutes before the alert. It was the most recent deploy, but checkout's errors were payments-svc timeouts two hops downstream.

## Resolution
{resolver} ran "Raise pool + restart payments-svc" without trying the failover first.

## Follow-ups
- CODEOWNERS review on services/payments-db/config.yaml, enforced in CI.
- Pool saturation alert at 80% (from {last_same}, still open).

pool_exhaustion.title: Third payments-db pool exhaustion: max_pool_size cut to {new}
pool_exhaustion.summary: {cause_author} lowered payments-db max_pool_size from {old} to {new} ({cfg}) to free connections for reconciliation-job. checkout-api errors reached {a1}, the third time after {prev_same}. Ignored a checkout-api deploy that landed {decoy_lag} minutes earlier, raised the pool back to {old} and restarted payments-svc.
timeline: Alert: checkout-api error rate {a1}. Sev1 opened.
Latest deploy is checkout-api {decoy_version} by {decoy_author}, but checkout's errors are payments-svc timeouts.
{cfg} lowered max_pool_size to {new}. Same cause as {prev_same}.
Ran 'Raise pool + restart payments-svc': max_pool_size back to {old}.
Checkout healthy for 10 minutes. Resolved in {duration} minutes, fastest of the three.

postmortem.title: payments-db pool exhaustion, third time
postmortem.body:
## Summary
Third pool exhaustion on payments-db ({prev_same}, now {id}). {cfg} lowered max_pool_size from {old} to {new}; checkout-api errors reached {a1}.

## Impact
Checkout failed for most shoppers for about 15 minutes.

## Root cause
{cause_author} lowered the pool to leave connections for reconciliation-job, which also connects to payments-db. Each of the three changes had a reasonable local motive; none knew the history.

## Red herring
checkout-api {decoy_version} ({decoy_deploy}) by {decoy_author} shipped {decoy_lag} minutes before the alert. The latest deploy is not the cause; the cause was two hops downstream on payments-db.

## Resolution
{resolver} ran "Raise pool + restart payments-svc" (3 out of 3 so far).

## Follow-ups
- Reject max_pool_size below 180 in config validation.
- Give reconciliation-job its own read replica instead of payments-db connections.

fraud_model_latency.title: fraud-svc latency from a heavier model in {version}
fraud_model_latency.summary: {deploy} ({version}) shipped a fraud model with three times the features; scoring p99 rose to {a0} and payments-svc p99 to {a1}. Switched to rules-only scoring, rolled back, then restored model scoring.
fraud_model_latency.commit: Ship gbm-2026-08 model with device and velocity features
timeline: Model inference time tripled after {deploy} loaded the new model.
Ran 'Switch fraud scoring to the rules-only fallback'.
payments-svc latency normal on rules-only scoring.
Set scoring_mode back to model, on the old model.

postmortem.title: New fraud model too slow for the charge path
postmortem.body:
## Summary
{deploy} ({version}) loaded a larger fraud model. Scoring p99 reached {a0}, which pushed payments-svc p99 to {a1}.

## Impact
Slow checkouts for 14 minutes, then 17 minutes of rules-only scoring with more manual reviews.

## Root cause
Commit {sha} by {cause_author} shipped a model benchmarked on a GPU box; production scores on CPU.

## Resolution
{resolver} switched to rules-only scoring with the runbook, rolled back, then restored model scoring.

## Follow-ups
- Latency budget check for models in CI, on production hardware.

gateway_timeout.title: api-gateway 504s after upstream timeout cut to {new} ms
gateway_timeout.summary: {cause_author} lowered api-gateway upstream_timeout_ms from {old} to {new} ({cfg}). checkout-api calls that wait on card authorization take up to 2 s, so the gateway cut them off with 504s ({a0} of requests). Restored {old} ms.
timeline: All errors are 504 on the checkout-api upstream; checkout-api logs show those requests completing after the client left.
{cfg} set upstream_timeout_ms to {new} {lag} minutes before the alert.

postmortem.title: Gateway timeout shorter than card authorization
postmortem.body:
## Summary
{cfg} lowered api-gateway upstream_timeout_ms from {old} to {new}. Checkouts that wait on the acquirer take up to 2 seconds and were cut off.

## Impact
{a0} of API calls returned 504 for {duration} minutes. Some charges completed after the shopper saw an error.

## Root cause
{cause_author} tuned the timeout for user-api and search-api; the setting is global.

## Resolution
{resolver} restored {old} ms with the runbook.

## Follow-ups
- Per-route upstream timeouts.
- Reconcile charges that completed after a 504.

ledger_consumer_stuck.title: ledger-svc stopped consuming payment events after {version}
ledger_consumer_stuck.summary: {deploy} ({version}) added a strict schema check that rejected events from an older producer; the consumer stopped at the first one and ledger lag reached {a0}. Rolled back and replayed from the stuck offset.
ledger_consumer_stuck.commit: Validate payment event schema version before posting entries
timeline: Consumer stuck on one offset; that event has schema version 3 and the new check only accepts 4.
The check came in {deploy}, deployed {lag} minutes before the alert.
Ran 'Replay missed payment events into ledger-svc' from the stuck offset.
Balance check job: merchant balances match payments-db totals.

postmortem.title: ledger-svc consumer blocked on an old event schema
postmortem.body:
## Summary
{deploy} ({version}) made ledger-svc reject payment events with schema version 3. The consumer stopped and ledger lag reached {a0}.

## Impact
Merchant balances were stale for {duration} minutes; payouts-svc held the 08:00 payout run.

## Root cause
Commit {sha} by {cause_author} assumed every producer was on schema version 4. payouts-svc still emits version 3 for adjustments.

## Resolution
{resolver} rolled back and replayed from the stuck offset.

## Follow-ups
- Dead-letter unknown schema versions instead of stopping the consumer.
- A second ledger-svc reviewer: only {resolver} knows the consumer code.

auth_key_expiry.title: auth-svc rejecting tokens: signing key expired
auth_key_expiry.summary: The auth-svc token signing key reached its 90-day expiry; new tokens failed validation at api-gateway and {a1} of API calls returned 401. Rotated to the next key with the runbook.
timeline: Alert: auth-svc error rate {a0}. Sev1 opened.
Tokens signed after 23:00 UTC fail validation; the active signing key expired at 23:00.
Ran 'Rotate the auth-svc token signing key'.
New tokens validate; 401s back to baseline. Resolved.

postmortem.title: Expired signing key, rotation not automated
postmortem.body:
## Summary
The auth-svc signing key expired at 23:00 UTC. For {duration} minutes newly issued tokens failed validation.

## Impact
{a1} of API calls failed with 401; merchants could not log in to the dashboard.

## Root cause
Key rotation every 90 days is manual and the calendar reminder went to someone who left.

## Resolution
{resolver} activated the next key with the runbook.

## Follow-ups
- Rotate keys automatically 7 days before expiry.
- Alert 14 days before any signing key expires.

kafka_disk_full.title: Kafka brokers near full disk after retention raised to {new} h
kafka_disk_full.summary: {cause_author} raised kafka retention_hours from {old} to {new} ({cfg}) for an analytics backfill. Local disk on two brokers reached {a0}, producers slowed and ledger-svc lag hit {a1}. Restored {old} h and moved partitions off the full brokers.
timeline: Brokers 2 and 4 above 90% disk; segment deletion stopped after {cfg} raised retention to {new} h.
Set retention_hours back to {old}; old segments are deleting.
Ran 'Move partitions off a full Kafka broker' for brokers 2 and 4.
Brokers under 70% disk, ledger-svc lag zero. Resolved.

postmortem.title: Kafka retention raised without disk headroom
postmortem.body:
## Summary
{cfg} raised retention_hours from {old} to {new}. Brokers stopped deleting segments and two filled to {a0}.

## Impact
Produce latency rose for every service; ledger-svc lag reached {a1}. No events were lost.

## Root cause
{cause_author} raised retention for a one-off analytics backfill that should have read from tiered storage in object-store.

## Resolution
{resolver} restored {old} h and reassigned partitions with the runbook.

## Follow-ups
- Backfills read from tiered storage, never from longer broker retention.
- Disk alert per broker at 75%.

edge_waf_block.title: Edge WAF blocking legitimate checkouts after rule update
edge_waf_block.summary: {deploy} ({version}) shipped a WAF rule set that matched the mobile SDK's base64 payment payload as SQL injection; {a0} of requests got 403. Rolled back.
edge_waf_block.commit: Enable OWASP CRS 4 paranoia level 2 on /v1/*
timeline: Alert: edge error rate {a0}. Sev1 opened.
403s from the WAF on /v1/checkout, mobile SDK traffic only.
Rule update in {deploy}, {lag} minutes before the alert.

postmortem.title: WAF paranoia level 2 blocked mobile checkouts
postmortem.body:
## Summary
{deploy} ({version}) raised the WAF paranoia level. Mobile SDK checkout payloads matched SQL injection rules and got 403.

## Impact
{a0} of requests, all mobile checkouts, failed for {duration} minutes.

## Root cause
Commit {sha} by {cause_author} was tested against web traffic only.

## Resolution
Rolled back to {prev_version}.

## Follow-ups
- Run new WAF rules in detect mode for a week before block.

acquirer_timeout_config.title: Charges timing out after acquirer read timeout cut to {new} ms
acquirer_timeout_config.summary: {cause_author} lowered acquirer-gateway read_timeout_ms from {old} to {new} ({cfg}). Slow but valid authorizations were abandoned and payments-svc errors reached {a0}. Switching acquirers did not help; restoring {old} ms did.
timeline: acquirer-gateway reports read timeouts on Northbank. Looks like the Northbank outage in {last[acquirer_outage]}.
Ran 'Route card traffic to the backup acquirer'.
Same timeouts on Meridian, so the problem is on our side.
{cfg} lowered read_timeout_ms to {new} {lag} minutes before the alert; p95 authorization time is 1.4 s.

postmortem.title: Acquirer read timeout below real authorization time
postmortem.body:
## Summary
{cfg} lowered acquirer-gateway read_timeout_ms from {old} to {new}. About 1 in 30 authorizations takes longer than that and was abandoned.

## Impact
{a0} of charges failed for {duration} minutes.

## Root cause
{cause_author} lowered the timeout to fail fast during acquirer outages like {last[acquirer_outage]}, without checking the authorization time distribution.

## What did not work
The acquirer switch runbook (minute 12): it fixes acquirer outages, not our own timeouts.

## Resolution
{resolver} restored {old} ms and switched back to Northbank.

## Follow-ups
- Timeout changes on acquirer-gateway need the p99 authorization time in the review.

payouts_batch_failed.title: Merchant payouts batch failed after {version}
payouts_batch_failed.summary: {deploy} ({version}) sent payout amounts as decimal strings to the bank file builder, which expects integer cents; every payout in the 16:00 batch failed. Rolled back and re-ran the batch before the bank cutoff.
payouts_batch_failed.commit: Format payout amounts with the shared money helper
timeline: Alert: payouts-svc error rate {a0}: the 16:00 UTC payout batch failed.
Bank file validation error: amount '1250.00' is not an integer.
Payouts sent before the bank's 17:00 cutoff. Resolved.

postmortem.title: Payout amounts formatted as decimals
postmortem.body:
## Summary
{deploy} ({version}) formatted payout amounts as decimal strings. The bank file builder rejected the whole 16:00 batch.

## Impact
Payouts were 24 minutes late but made the bank cutoff. No merchant was paid twice.

## Root cause
Commit {sha} by {cause_author} reused a money helper meant for display.

## Resolution
{resolver} rolled back and re-ran the batch.

## Follow-ups
- Validate the bank file in CI against the bank's schema.

webhooks_bad_deploy.title: Webhook signatures invalid after {version}
webhooks_bad_deploy.summary: {deploy} ({version}) re-serialized webhook bodies after signing them, so merchant signature checks failed on {a0} of deliveries. Rolled back; failed deliveries were retried.
webhooks_bad_deploy.commit: Pretty-print webhook payloads for easier debugging
timeline: Merchants return 401 invalid signature; since {deploy} the signed bytes differ from the sent bytes.
Retries delivered; error rate normal. Resolved.

postmortem.title: Pretty-printing broke webhook signatures
postmortem.body:
## Summary
{deploy} ({version}) pretty-printed webhook bodies after computing the signature. Merchants verifying signatures rejected {a0} of deliveries.

## Impact
Webhooks to merchants that verify signatures failed for {duration} minutes; all were redelivered.

## Root cause
Commit {sha} by {cause_author} changed serialization in the sender, not the signer.

## Resolution
Rolled back to {prev_version}.

## Follow-ups
- Sign the exact bytes sent; test with a real verifier.

fraud_false_declines.title: False fraud declines after block threshold lowered to {new}
fraud_false_declines.summary: {cause_author} lowered fraud-svc block_threshold from {old} to {new} ({cfg}), meaning to change the review queue. About one charge in fifteen was blocked as fraud and payments-svc declines reached {a0}. Restored {old}.
timeline: Declines are fraud_blocked with scores between 0.6 and 0.85; the model's score distribution is unchanged.
{cfg} set block_threshold to {new} {lag} minutes before the alert; review_threshold is also 0.6.

postmortem.title: Block threshold set to the review threshold
postmortem.body:
## Summary
{cfg} lowered fraud-svc block_threshold from {old} to {new}. Charges that should have gone to manual review were declined.

## Impact
{a0} of charges were declined as fraud for {duration} minutes.

## Root cause
{cause_author} edited block_threshold instead of review_threshold; the two keys sit next to each other.

## Resolution
{resolver} restored {old}.

## Follow-ups
- Validate block_threshold > review_threshold + 0.1.

redis_primary_down.title: redis-cache primary unreachable
redis_primary_down.summary: The redis-cache primary host lost its network interface; every Redis call failed, auth-svc errors hit {a1} and checkout-api, webhooks-svc and pricing-svc degraded. Promoted the replica with the runbook.
timeline: Alert: redis-cache error rate {a0}. Sev1 opened.
Primary does not answer PING from two hosts; the replica is healthy. No recent change on redis-cache.
Restarted auth-svc, checkout-api and webhooks-svc to drop the old primary address.

postmortem.title: redis-cache primary host network failure
postmortem.body:
## Summary
The redis-cache primary became unreachable after a host NIC failure. Everything that uses Redis degraded until the replica was promoted.

## Impact
auth-svc failed {a1} of requests for {duration} minutes; checkout-api, webhooks-svc and pricing-svc were degraded.

## Root cause
Hardware: NIC failure on the primary host. Sentinel did not fail over because two sentinels ran on that host.

## Resolution
{resolver} promoted the replica by hand and restarted clients that pin the primary address.

## Follow-ups
- Spread sentinels across three hosts.
- Clients resolve the primary through sentinel, not a fixed address.

schema_registry_reject.title: Kafka rejecting payment events after schema-registry {version}
schema_registry_reject.summary: {deploy} ({version}) changed schema-registry's subject naming, so brokers could not find the schema for payment-events and rejected every produced record. payments-svc errors reached {a0}. Rolled back.
timeline: Alert: payments-svc error rate {a0}. Sev1 opened.
payments-svc produce calls fail with INVALID_RECORD: no schema for subject payment-events-value.
schema-registry {version} ({deploy}) changed the subject naming strategy {lag} minutes before the alert.

postmortem.title: Subject naming change broke broker-side schema validation
postmortem.body:
## Summary
{deploy} ({version}) switched schema-registry to RecordNameStrategy. Brokers validate every record against the registry and could no longer find the payment-events schema.

## Impact
payments-svc failed {a0} of charges and checkout-api {a1} for {duration} minutes: charges are rolled back when the payment event cannot be produced.

## Root cause
Commit {sha} by {cause_author} was tested with clients only. Kafka depends on schema-registry for every produced record, not only for new schemas.

## Resolution
Rolled back to {prev_version}.

## Follow-ups
- Staging test that produces through brokers with validation on.

reconciliation_mismatch.title: Reconciliation reporting false mismatches after {version}
reconciliation_mismatch.summary: {deploy} ({version}) compared settlement amounts in the acquirer's currency against ledger amounts in the merchant's currency; {a0} of lines were flagged as mismatched. Rolled back and re-ran the job.
reconciliation_mismatch.commit: Compare settlement lines using the presentment amount
timeline: Every flagged line is a cross-currency charge.
Rolled reconciliation-job back to {prev_version} and re-ran last night's batch.

postmortem.title: Reconciliation compared amounts in different currencies
postmortem.body:
## Summary
{deploy} ({version}) compared settlement and ledger amounts in different currencies, flagging {a0} of lines.

## Impact
The finance team got a false mismatch report; no money moved.

## Root cause
Commit {sha} by {cause_author} used the presentment amount; settlement files carry the settlement currency.

## Resolution
{resolver} rolled back and re-ran the batch.

## Follow-ups
- Cross-currency fixtures in the reconciliation tests.

inventory_n_plus_one.title: inventory-svc N+1 queries after {version}
inventory_n_plus_one.summary: {deploy} ({version}) loaded reservations one SKU at a time instead of in one query; inventory-svc p99 reached {a0} and inventory-db saturation {a1}. Rolled back.
inventory_n_plus_one.commit: Load reservations through the new repository layer
timeline: Queries per request up from 2 to about 40 since {deploy}.
Not the missing index from {last[inventory_index_dropped]}: indexes are intact, there are just many more queries.

postmortem.title: Repository layer issued one query per SKU
postmortem.body:
## Summary
{deploy} ({version}) moved reservation loading to a repository layer that queries per SKU. inventory-svc p99 reached {a0}.

## Impact
Slow checkouts for {duration} minutes; no failures.

## Root cause
Commit {sha} by {cause_author}: the new repository layer lacks a batch load method.

## Resolution
Rolled back to {prev_version}.

postmortem.body:
## Summary
{deploy} upgraded the KRaft controllers to {version}. One node restarted with an outdated voters list and the quorum split.

## Impact
Kafka produce errors reached {a0} for {duration} minutes; payments-svc p99 rose to {a1}. Every service on kafka was affected.

Commit {sha} by {cause_author} set the new bootstrap setting but left the old static voters list on controller 3.

## Resolution

## Summary

## Impact
Webhooks were late for {duration} minutes; none were lost.

## Root cause
Delivery workers are shared across merchants with no per-merchant concurrency limit.

## Resolution
{resolver} paused the endpoint and drained the backlog with the runbook.

## Follow-ups
- Per-merchant concurrency limits in webhooks-svc.

ledger-svc skipped 312 events on statement timeouts during the slow period.
Ran 'Replay missed payment events into ledger-svc' for the skipped range.

postmortem.title: Autovacuum could not keep up with month-end volume
postmortem.body:
## Summary
ledger_entries bloated after the month-end spike; ledger-db p99 reached {a0} and ledger-svc fell {a1} behind, skipping 312 events on timeouts.

## Impact
Merchant balances were stale for {duration} minutes and 312 entries were missing until the replay.

## Root cause
Autovacuum cost limits were sized for normal days. ledger-svc skips an event on a statement timeout instead of retrying.

## Resolution
{resolver} vacuumed by hand and replayed the skipped events with the runbook.

## Follow-ups
- Raise autovacuum limits for ledger_entries before month end.
- ledger-svc retries on statement timeout instead of skipping.
